title: One person, six risk tests
hook: Should one risk score predict all six of your choices?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast domain-specific elicited risk preferences with a single stable risk ranking.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast domain-specific elicited risk preferences with a single stable risk ranking.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Toy test A ranks three people 1, 2, 3. Test B ranks them 3, 2, 1. What is the correlation? Toy inputs A=[3, 2, 1]; B=[1, 2, 3].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[-1, 3, 1], [1, 1, 3]]. Labels: Rank correlation, Person 1 B, Person 3 B.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The same people can receive opposite rankings under these two toy measurements. Agreement across elicitation methods is an empirical question; a stable ordering cannot simply be assumed from using the same word, risk, in each task.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Test B person 1=1, Test B person 2=2, Test B person 3=3. What is Rank correlation? Answer: 1.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Test B person 1=1, Test B person 2=2, Test B person 3=3. What is Rank correlation?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 1. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Risk preferences measured six different ways in the same people barely correlated (Pedroni et al., 2017).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast domain-specific elicited risk preferences with a single stable risk ranking.
